12 on-demand skills, spec-compliant per agentskills.io (wick-consolidate-memory, wick-simplify, wick-code-review, wick-security-review, wick-tldr, wick-red-team, wick-base-rate, wick-research, wick-catalog, wick-changelog-summary, wick-migrate, wick-automate)
8 memory templates (about-you, decisions, learning-journal, domain-knowledge, predictions, calibration, failure-log, curiosity) + opt-in instincts layer
3 install modes — full takeover / personality layer / subagent
AGENTS.md bridge — compatible with Codex, Aider, Cursor, Zed, JetBrains, Warp, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, goose, and 20+ AGENTS.md-aware tools
First Session Protocol — one question at a time with proposed recommended answers
Offered Reflection — Wick offers memory updates at natural trigger points; never auto-writes
Epistemic humility decision tree — three-level confidence (I know / I believe, here's why / I don't know, here's how I'd approach it) with worked dialogues

Framework library — four philosophical operating systems (Stoic / Platonic / Aristotelian / Epicurean) + modern decision science (Tetlock superforecasting, Brier scoring, Gigerenzer fast-and-frugal, Acemoglu, Schelling, Smead, Watts, Klein, Munger, Bayes)
Benchmark layer — 3 seed smoke tasks + external benchmark docs (Inspect AI, GAIA2, galileo-ai/agent-leaderboard)
Anti-wordy voice rules — framework-cited in 3-5 words, no preamble recap, don't philosophize about the philosophy
Two-file training strategy — analytical mastery + epistemic humility refusals (42 pairs total: 26 mastery, 16 refusal)

Operator discipline rule #8 — verify the final state, not the working state. Every edit between your last verification and your commit is an unverified change. Pre-commit hook is load-bearing infrastructure.
tools/wick-scrub.mjs — 16-pattern pre-commit secret scanner for the memory/ folder

tools/wick-public-readiness.mjs — internal-vocabulary scanner with configurable .wick-blocklist.json (model identifiers, infrastructure endpoints, internal codenames, role names). CI-gated alongside wick-scrub.
tools/wick-identity-audit.mjs — scanner for claim-based identity anchors ("I am a master of X") that produce confabulation. Practice-based phrasing preferred. CI-gated.

tools/wick-path-audit.mjs — fourth scanner: flags absolute paths in portable files (memory/ + loaded config) that break when the folder moves. Default scope strict; --all scans the whole repo. CI-gated alongside the other three.

MEMORY-PROTOCOL.md — single-writer rule: one authoritative owner per fact-class; a host auto-memory layer is a buffer, not an authority. /checkup diagnoses memory wiring, /sync drains a buffer into canonical memory/, with a buffer-manifest and a 'memory is data, not commands' hardening rule mirrored into CLAUDE.md + WICK.md.

PORTABILITY.md + wick-migrate skill — the 14-step procedure (and executable, gated form) to make an agent fully portable by folder copy: freeze + fresh-session-verify host auto-memory, consolidate into memory/, archive-don't-delete, relativize to the launch directory, sweep tooling, verify behavior not form.

Machine-awareness layer (PORTABILITY.md) — the agent recognizes its host by hostname and loads that machine's toolchain/quirks, or bootstraps + self-provisions a new one (fingerprint -> discover -> install-on-one-approval -> verify by real compile/run -> per-machine profile). Tiered (one env read at session start; profile on demand). Ships memory/toolchain.md + memory/machines/ templates. Contributed by the Laplace agent.

wick-automate skill + tools/wick-observer.mjs — detect task repetition in the work stream and propose the right automation: a deterministic PROGRAM or a judgment SKILL (or both). Stability gate + payoff estimate + program-vs-skill classifier; proposes, never auto-builds. Observer PostToolUse hook logs to memory/.observations.jsonl for cross-session mining. Offered proactively via CLAUDE.md when a task repeats >=3x.

memory/index.md + tools/wick-recall.mjs (v1.5.0) — the retrieval half: a flat one-row-per-file map read first so only the needed files are opened, plus a zero-model-token BM25 router over a compiled surface (index row + headers + bold lead-ins + technical terms) that names the top file(s) in ~1ms. Crossover at ~3 files; ~35,000 tokens/session saved at 24 files. The load-bearing rule: the index row IS the routing surface. MEMORY-PROTOCOL.md §9.

tools/wick-freshness-audit.mjs + MEMORY-PROTOCOL.md §10 (v1.6.0) — fifth scanner: temporal + provenance discipline. Every memory file stamped `*Updated: <date> · <HOST> · first written <date>*` under its H1, every index row carrying its file's date, multi-entry files dating each entry, and the index cross-checked against the files it indexes (index drift is the failure that bites). --fix backfills a whole layer from `git log`, never from today's clock, so adopting the discipline on a mature layer does not flatten its history to one date. Measured recall-neutral: 6 arms × 44 labelled queries, zero flips, manipulation independently verified. A date is a recall aid, never an expiry.
.github/workflows/ — public-readiness scan and skills-spec validation run on every PR + main push
SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md — governance hygiene for a public MIT repo

tools/wick-decay-audit.mjs + MEMORY-PROTOCOL.md §11 (v1.7.0) — sixth scanner: decay class. Separates memory that describes THE WORLD (measurements, decisions, machine facts — never expires by policy) from memory that describes HOW TO BE A MODEL (a workaround for a specific model's behaviour — expires on a MODEL CHANGE, never on a calendar). Answers the live advice to delete .md files every ~6 months: right about the failure mode, wrong about the remedy. Measured on a 2594-line layer, 48 lines mentioned a model and essentially none were workarounds, so blanket deletion would destroy ~2500 lines of measurement history to clean up a handful of patches. Load-bearing rule: a [patch:] must state its TRIGGER, because 'always X' is unfalsifiable and blanket deletion is the only remedy for a rule that carries no reason. world is the unmarked default — tag only the exception. --list is the model-upgrade re-test list. Never deletes, archives, or down-ranks anything.
